Gaissau-Hintersee is a Salzburg-area mountain network with village access and varied forested regional terrain.
Hesselbach is a small German local ski slope whose simple lift-served layout is oriented toward learning and nearby residents.
Kurza Góra is a modern Polish regional ski centre with groomed slopes, learning facilities and an accessible day-area format.
Nauders is an Austrian resort near the Reschen Pass with high alpine terrain and a family-oriented Tyrolean base.

Storklinten emphasizes prepared pistes for beginners, recreational skiers and more committed riders, with places to stay on the mountain. Its snow-storage program supports early-season preparation; cross-country skiing and other outdoor activities are separate offerings.

Ski Smithers is a northern British Columbia mountain area with forested lift-served terrain and a strong community connection.

ov.text: Snowstar pairs local ski and snowboard lanes with a substantial freestyle offering. Lessons, rentals and on-site dining make it a self-contained winter outing near the Quad Cities; tubing is a separate activity rather than part of the ski-run total.

Ski Sundown packs a broad difficulty range into a compact Connecticut ski area. More than half its trails are classed as easier, with a mile-long easy route and freestyle features on two trails adding progression options.
Ski Sunne offers a compact Swedish slope network with a practical family and progression focus.

Ski Valley offers skiing and snowboarding on beginner, intermediate and advanced routes, with rentals and certified instruction available. Its school-group programs make learning a clear part of the experience, alongside ordinary recreational laps.

ov.text: Ski Ward’s short vertical and nine-trail network make it a compact Massachusetts option for learning and repeat laps. A substantial snow-school offering complements beginner, intermediate and expert trails, with tubing treated separately.

Dorfgastein is a family-oriented entry to the connected Dorfgastein–Grossarltal area, with gentle slopes suited to first turns. Its local profile should be read separately from the larger Gastein pass network and its other learning parks.

ov.text: Filzmoos spreads its skiing over Rossbrand and Grossberg, with a village-scale layout and an emphasis on relaxed family days. The mountain backdrop and space for cruising distinguish it from the much larger connected networks elsewhere in Ski amadé.

Grossarl opens onto the connected Grossarltal–Dorfgastein slopes, combining groomed skiing with mountain-hut stops and playful ski attractions. The shared two-valley network is larger than Grossarl’s local sector, so its totals are not assigned here alone.

ov.text: Hochkönig links skiing between Maria Alm, Dienten and Mühlbach, combining broad pistes with mountain-hut stops and panoramic touring circuits. Additional areas included on the pass should not be confused with the continuously linked core.

Klínovec combines an interconnected piste network with dedicated learning facilities and ski and snowboard instruction. Its chairlifts, surface lifts and children’s conveyors serve different needs; the wider cross-resort pass covers more terrain than this local mountain inventory.
Skiarena Silbersattel is a compact Thuringian Forest ski area with groomed local slopes and a regional winter-sports focus.
Hinterstoder Höss is an Upper Austrian mountain area with developed alpine pistes and a strong racing and regional-resort identity.
Mühlwiese is a compact German local ski slope near Osterode, focused on community winter recreation.

ov.text: Ski Land is a nonprofit, community-supported hill with an upside-down layout: the visitor starts high and skis down before riding back up. Its Silver Star Express provides a substantial local vertical without the scale or services of a large resort village.
Albstadt-Tailfingen Ski Lift is a small Swabian Alb slope operated for local winter recreation when natural conditions allow.

ov.text: Skimore Oslo offers a city-accessible ski day with learning areas, terrain parks and floodlit slopes. Visitors can buy a day pass rather than a membership, making it an option for occasional outings as well as regular local skiing.
SkiPark Magura is a forested Polish mountain area with groomed regional slopes on Magura Małastowska.

ov.text: Angertal Ski Center is a learning-focused Gastein base with broad practice terrain and direct links into the surrounding mountain network.
Simmelsberg is a small Rhön ski centre whose wooded slopes and local club culture support training and short winter outings.
Skolnity is a developed ski area above central Wisła with convenient access and scenic Beskid slopes.
Sky Resort is a developed ski area near Ulaanbaatar, offering convenient groomed terrain in a cold, open steppe-edge setting.

ov.text: Sky Valley combines gentle woodland practice with intermediate cruising, freestyle features and demanding upper moguls. A longer descent reaches the ski center, but beginners are advised to return on the access lift instead of skiing that route.
Słotwiny Arena is a developed ski and bike area at Krynica-Zdrój with groomed regional slopes and modern visitor facilities.
Słotwiny is one of Krynica-Zdrój’s ski sectors, with groomed local slopes and convenient resort-town access.
Smiggin Holes is a sheltered Perisher base with approachable slopes, lodging and lift links into the wider Australian resort network.
Śnieżnica is a forested Polish mountain area at Kasina Wielka with a substantial regional descent.

Snow Creek brings a compact ski area to the bluffs of the Missouri River. Its trail mix is mostly intermediate, with a terrain park and full published snowmaking coverage supporting the local winter offering.

Onze combines coastal views over Ishikari Bay with short forest, family and sporting runs. Evening skiing adds views of city lights, while steeper pitches and a mogul course provide a different challenge from the gentler Panorama and Family slopes.

Ogna Hotaka combines the broad, gentle Romance course with steeper carving runs and designated ungroomed terrain. The contrast between relaxed group cruising and more technical snow gives different abilities distinct parts of the mountain to explore.
Snow Park Dorogawa is a compact Nara-area snow hill offering modest lift-served terrain in a quiet mountain-valley setting.

Snow Resort Nekoyama is a regional Hiroshima mountain with groomed family runs and a relaxed day-trip character.

ov.text: Snowriver combines Jackson Creek Summit and Black River Basin, linked by a shuttle rather than ski trails. Cruisers, mogul runs and wooded terrain give the two hills variety, while the main base at Jackson Creek carries the fuller range of visitor services.

Snow Space Salzburg links Flachau, Wagrain and Alpendorf into a large piste network. Its connected layout supports exploring between resort bases; the additional connection to neighboring ski areas is a wider offering, not part of these local network totals.

Snow Valley in Southern California has an intermediate-and-advanced-heavy winter trail mix and terrain-park options. It is a separate mountain from Snow Summit, and the similarly named Edmonton hill has no connection to these measurements.

Snow World Züschen is a compact Sauerland ski area with local groomed slopes and a practical day-trip character.

ov.text: Snowbasin combines 115 trails, thirteen lifts and 3,000 skiable acres. That gives it a large terrain footprint with an extensive marked-trail network to explore.

Snowhaven is a city-owned local ski hill near Grangeville, oriented around weekends and selected holidays. The downhill offering includes a T-bar and a beginner rope tow; nearby cross-country trails and the tubing hill are separate activities.

ov.text: Snowy Range offers a contained high-elevation ski area in Wyoming’s Medicine Bow setting, with learning slopes and more challenging terrain. Its mountain scale is clearer from the skiable acreage than from the inconsistent published vertical and trail counts.
Sol-Fa Oda is a small Japanese regional ski area with straightforward groomed terrain and a quiet local-mountain atmosphere.
Soliabacken is a small Swedish ski hill near Norsjö, serving community recreation and local training.

ov.text: Edelweiss combines a local Outaouais ski outing with a strong learning focus. Two dedicated beginner areas and a covered carpet support first turns, while the wider mountain offers progression beyond the learning slopes.
Sommet Gabriel is a compact Laurentian mountain whose approachable runs and local atmosphere suit shorter ski days.

Song Mountain offers local skiing with a restaurant at the base and a shared pass relationship with Labrador. They remain two separate hills: a ticket partnership does not turn Labrador’s trails or vertical into Song Mountain statistics.
Sonnenlifte Röfleuten/Halden is a small Allgäu ski area with family slopes and convenient village access.
Sorochany is a modern Moscow-region ski center with multiple compact slopes designed for frequent day and evening sessions.
Soszów is a forested Wisła ski area with a traditional Beskid layout and regional day-resort character.

Speikboden combines broad pistes, high-mountain learning spaces and more sporting Sonnklar descents with views toward the Dolomites. Its local terrain offers a varied day without including neighboring Klausberg or the separate sledding routes in the skiing totals.
Spielbergalm is a small Salzburg mountain area where modest lift-served slopes and an alpine setting shape a relaxed ski day.

ov.text: Spirit Mountain combines a substantial Midwest vertical with freestyle terrain and beginner facilities above Duluth. Its two chalet areas divide visitor services between the top and bottom, while Nordic skiing has its own separate trail network.
Sport Dolina is an urban Polish ski centre designed for convenient local instruction and short groomed sessions.

Sportgastein combines high-altitude piste skiing with a pronounced freeride identity. Marked ski routes and an information base support that adventurous side, but off-piste access still calls for appropriate equipment, judgment and a current conditions check.
Spout Springs is an Oregon mountain ski area with a compact, independent layout in the Blue Mountains.
Spring Valley Sendai Izumi is an urban-accessible Miyagi ski area serving day visitors, learners and evening sessions.
St. Jakob is an East Tyrol ski area with high alpine slopes and a quiet valley setting away from major resort corridors.

ov.text: St. Jakob combines open mountain skiing with family descents, a learning lift and a funpark. Timed and training runs give sporting skiers extra variety, while snowmaking supports the valley descents without guaranteeing daily availability.
St. Mary Ski Area is a regional Tohoku hill with a practical mix of family slopes, progression terrain and straightforward lift access.

Stara Planina combines gondola-accessed skiing at Jabucko Raviste with the Babin Zub sectors. Learning facilities and varied pistes sit in a striking rocky mountain setting; the surrounding peaks are not treated as lift-served ski elevations.

ov.text: Stari Vrh offers varied skiing in the hills around Škofja Loka, with terrain for learners and stronger skiers. Night skiing and a separate snow park with a learning conveyor add options for shorter sessions and family outings.
Staroměstsko is a Czech mountain-region ski identity covering local slopes around Staré Město rather than one single resort pod.

Camurac offers a small family ski setting among the forests and ridges of the Aude Pyrenees. It is a mountain for a contained downhill outing rather than a large linked circuit; current terrain measurements still need an operator inventory.

ov.text: Val d’Allos – La Foux is a southern-Alps resort base with high open slopes and links across the Espace Lumière domain.

Les Rousses offers cross-border Jura skiing across Dôle/Tuffes and La Serra, moving through forests and open combes. Easy learning terrain and more technical black runs share views toward the Alps and Lake Geneva; the Nordic network remains separate.

Granier is a very small Chartreuse station where learning, sledding and a community snow day matter more than vertical scale.

Stevens Pass balances a largely intermediate trail mix with demanding Cascade steeps and chutes. Evening skiing adds another way to use the mountain, while the separate Nordic center does not contribute to the alpine terrain total.
Stok is a compact ski area in Wisła with groomed local terrain and convenient resort-town access.

Stożek is a forested Beskid ski area above Wisła with a compact lift network and a more traditional mountain feel.

Suche is a small Podhale ski area with groomed family terrain and convenient access near Zakopane.

Sugadaira spreads a broad selection of courses across three areas, with learning terrain, training slopes and views toward the Northern Alps. Some transfers use a shuttle, so its published size should not be read as one continuously linked mountain.

Sugar Bowl links four Donner Summit peaks with open groomers and sheltered tree skiing. Its snowbound village gives it a distinctive base-area feel, while neighboring Royal Gorge is a separate Nordic destination and is not part of the downhill acreage.

Suhara Ski Area offers a regional snow-country experience with groomed family terrain and a quieter pace than large destination resorts.

Now called Saskadena Six, this historic Vermont hill combines a small lift network with a long tradition of community skiing and racing. Family learning terrain sits alongside more challenging options; the old Suicide Six name remains only as an identity reference.
Suishōzan Ski Area is a small Akita community hill where uncomplicated groomed slopes support lessons and local recreation.

Summit Pass is Timberline’s lower, beginner-focused area in Government Camp, with gentle slopes, lessons and a lodge. Its own ticket is not equivalent to full Timberline access, and the upper resort’s headline vertical should not be assigned to this learning hill.

Sunday River is a sprawling Maine ski network built around eight connected peaks. Cruisers, glades and a large snowmaking system favor exploring different sectors through the day rather than treating the resort as one uniform slope.

Sunnegga is a Zermatt mountain sector reached rapidly from town, with sunny pistes and exceptional Matterhorn views.

ov.text: Sunridge is an Edmonton hill with learning carpets, chair-served skiing, terrain parks and a skier-cross offering. Its emphasis on lessons and community events makes it a local progression spot, with tubing kept separate from the downhill experience.

ov.text: Sunvalley forms an entrance to Shiga Kogen, with lodging nearby and intermediate and steeper slopes alongside a short beginner option. Connections with Maruike and Hasuike make it suitable for moving between several smaller sectors in one day.
Suomu is a Finnish Lapland ski resort with compact fell terrain, woodland runs and a quiet destination atmosphere.
Super Besse is a developed Massif Central resort with open volcanic slopes and a broad range of regional winter facilities.
Super-Châtel is a village-facing sector above Châtel, offering local slopes and connections toward the wider Portes du Soleil.
Superbagnères is a historic Pyrenees ski area above Luchon, with high mountain views and several distinct terrain sectors.
SuperDévoluy combines a slopeside resort base with broad, sunny terrain and links across the wider Dévoluy ski area.
Sveitsi is a compact Finnish ski centre at Hyvinkää, designed for lessons, local laps and convenient southern access.
Swiss Village is a small Japanese ski area in Kyoto Prefecture with a simple regional layout and local winter character.

ov.text: Szczyrk Mountain Resort spreads varied downhill runs across the Silesian Beskids, with illuminated terrain extending the day into evening skiing. Gondola and chairlift upgrades support its local network, which is smaller than the combined area available through the shared pass.
Szklana Góra is a compact Polish ski area at Harbutowice with groomed family terrain and modern local facilities.
Szwajcaria Bałtowska is a compact Polish recreation centre with family skiing and a purpose-built visitor base.
Szymoszkowa is a Zakopane ski slope with convenient town access and broad views toward the High Tatras.
Tahko is a major Finnish ski centre with numerous groomed slopes, a developed village and a lively regional destination feel.
Taiheizan Ski Resort Opas is an Akita-area community mountain offering groomed slopes, learning facilities and convenient regional access.

Tainai mixes long, gentle woodland skiing with a much steeper Challenge course. Forest and sea views, a learning conveyor and scheduled night skiing give it a varied character beyond its beginner-friendly lower slopes.

Taira combines a compact set of sporting slopes with a gentle Enjoy course for newcomers. A dedicated mogul course and competition activity add a technical side, while the children’s park has its own conveyor.
Takamagahara Mammoth Ski Area is a broad Shiga Kogen sector with open cruising, family terrain and direct connections toward neighboring areas.
Takamine Mountain Park is a high Nagano ski area, formerly known as Asama 2000, with open slopes and a mountain-focused atmosphere.
Takanbō Ski Slopes is a small Gokayama hill whose snow-country setting and uncomplicated local slopes define the visit.

ov.text: Takasu combines long beginner-friendly connections with ridge cruising, steep mogul terrain and extensive freestyle features. Its terrain ranges from broad practice slopes to the demanding Champion descent; neighboring Dynaland is a separate part of the shared mountain offering.

Tangram combines hotel-oriented skiing with designated ungroomed and tree-run terrain on Mount Madarao’s north-northwest side. Most courses return toward the main hotel, while a separate shared pass allows exploration of neighboring Madarao without merging the two inventories.

Tateshina Tokyu Ski Resort is a compact resort hill focused on family skiing, instruction and easy access from nearby accommodation.

Tauplitzalm is an Austrian plateau resort with broad alpine terrain and links between its high slopes and valley access points.
Tazawako is an Akita ski area with varied mountain terrain and expansive views toward its namesake lake.
Tegatayama is a small Akita ski hill oriented toward community use, instruction and short regional sessions.

Tendō Kogen is a small Yamagata highland ski area focused on accessible family terrain and community winter use.
Tengu Kogen is a high Shikoku ski area with open plateau scenery and a distinctive southern-Japan setting.

ov.text: Terakoya offers a high-mountain panorama and a compact network of upper slopes. Its onward forest connection leads through other sectors toward Giant, but that longer shared journey should not be confused with Terakoya’s own local dimensions.
Termas de Chillán is a Chilean Andes resort where volcanic terrain, forested lower slopes and hot-spring lodging shape the destination.
Termignon is a traditional Val Cenis village sector with forested access into the larger linked ski domain.
Terre Ronde is a modest Plateau d’Hauteville alpine area suited to learning and regional snow days rather than long mountain journeys.

ov.text: Teton Pass in Montana offers a small lift network and a clear distinction between chair-served skiing and higher backcountry terrain. The Big Bear chair provides the lift-served drop; the additional vertical above it requires hiking and is not part of an ordinary lift lap.

ov.text: The Summit at Snoqualmie comprises several connected Summit areas plus the separate Alpental mountain. That combination supports varied skiing and extensive evening access, but a resort-wide number should not be mistaken for one continuous lift lap.
Thollon-les-Mémises sits high above Lake Geneva, pairing compact lift-served terrain with unusually broad lake views.

Thunder Ridge is a local New York hill with gentle learning slopes, more demanding trails and evening skiing. A sizeable carpet-lift provision complements the chairlifts, helping keep introductory sessions distinct from laps on the main runs.

ov.text: Thunderhill is a volunteer-supported Swan Valley ski area with upper and lower T-bar-served slopes. Groomed downhill runs and night skiing anchor the winter offering, while the small Nordic network is counted separately.

ov.text: Tignes le Lac is a central high-altitude resort base with immediate access to the linked Tignes–Val d’Isère terrain.
Le Lavachet is a residential Tignes sector with convenient access to the resort’s high-altitude lift network.

ov.text: Tikjda is an Algerian mountain resort in the Djurdjura with dramatic limestone scenery and conditions-dependent snow terrain.

Timber Ridge in Michigan offers short lift laps across beginner hills, intermediate slopes and wooded terrain. More demanding runs and several freestyle parks extend the options beyond first turns, with tubing kept outside the ski-trail description.

ov.text: Timberline combines open upper-mountain skiing with forested runs and freestyle terrain on Mount Hood. Its longest advertised descent finishes at Summit Pass and requires shuttle logistics; Palmer access can be by chair or snowcat, depending on operations.

ov.text: Titcomb is a compact Maine community mountain with beginner instruction, a freestyle park and selected evening skiing. Its alpine slopes are separate from the longer Nordic trail network, so cross-country kilometers do not inflate the downhill offering.

Titus spreads its Adirondack foothill skiing across three peaks with two lodges and slopeside cabins. Its headline count combines trails, glades and features, giving a sense of variety rather than fifty conventional groomed runs.
Tochio Family is a community learning hill focused on gentle slopes, children and uncomplicated practice.
Toga is a compact Toyama mountain ski area with a remote village setting and regional character.

mf.label: Listed lifts
mf.note: Includes the two Chusha lifts with limited operating dates.

ov.text: Togakushi offers mountain views and a broad spread of difficulty, from first-turn terrain to courses aimed at experienced competitors. Its learning options and more demanding runs make it a mixed-ability mountain, with some sectors operating on limited schedules.

Togari’s Earth Dragon and Sky Dragon fields mix gentle woodland cruising with mogul practice, freestyle features and steeper ungroomed slopes. Its renamed course network gives different abilities distinct places to explore without treating every connecting run as a major descent.
Tokusagamine is a small Yamaguchi mountain snow area with local lift-served terrain and a regional winter focus.
Tre Nevi is an Abruzzo regional ski identity grouping mountain areas rather than describing one continuous lift network.
Trije Kralji is a Slovenian Pohorje ski area with forested regional slopes and a quiet mountain base.
Trillevallen is a Swedish mountain resort with a quieter family character and lift-served terrain near the Åre region.

ov.text: Troll pairs T-bar skiing with long groomers, wooded runs and a community-oriented base. The newer Pinegrove terrain adds mainly advanced descents, while the original mountain still includes a dedicated beginner hill.
Tschindirtschero is a mountain ski resort identity in Dagestan with lift-served terrain in a remote Caucasus setting.
Tsey is a Caucasus mountain resort in North Ossetia with dramatic valley scenery and lift-served alpine terrain.
Tsigov Chark is a Bulgarian mountain resort area near Batak Reservoir with compact regional ski facilities.

Tsugaike combines an exceptionally broad, gentle lower slope with longer routes higher on the mountain. Its varied pitches offer room to progress beyond first turns, making the mountain suitable for mixed-ability groups as well as family learning days.

Tufandagh combines a beginner area with longer intermediate descents and steeper expert slopes above Gabala. Several ropeways connect different mountain levels, with sightseeing access extending below the ski terrain itself.

ov.text: Turini–Camp d’Argent is a small southern-Alps station with open pass terrain and a distinctly Mediterranean hinterland setting.
Turnia is a compact Bukowina Tatrzańska ski area with approachable slopes and local resort access.

Tūroa spreads across a volcanic landscape on Mount Ruapehu, with open runs, natural half-pipes and off-trail options. Intermediate terrain forms the largest share of its published mix, alongside learning facilities and more demanding descents.

Tussey is a small local mountain focused on skiing progression near State College. The former tubing hill has been returned to ski and snowboard use to make more room for beginners and intermediates, so tubing is no longer part of the winter offering.
Tylicz Ski is a family-oriented mountain area with groomed slopes and a developed base near Krynica-Zdrój.
Uenohara is a small Japanese ski area near Daisen with a local mountain layout and regional winter focus.
Ukkohalla is a Finnish resort with compact fell skiing, a developed base and a broad year-round recreation identity.
Ullådalen is a quieter Åre mountain sector with access to the wider resort network and a more natural valley setting.
Unazuki Snow Park is a small Toyama slope that pairs local skiing with access to the wider hot-spring destination.
Unterstmatt is a compact Black Forest ski area with local groomed slopes near the Schwarzwaldhochstraße.

ov.text: Up Kannabe puts broad learning slopes and family practice at the center of the experience. The steeper North Wall offers a contrast, while a long beginner conveyor and scheduled evening skiing help groups build a day around their confidence and pace.

Ushidake combines a long downhill route with a snowpark on the upper West course. Night skiing adds an evening option, making the mountain suitable for a mix of regular laps and freestyle practice when the relevant areas are open.
Utopia Saioto is a regional Hiroshima ski area with developed snow terrain and a practical day-resort character.

Val Cenis links three villages beneath a largely north-facing ski domain, with views toward the Mont Cenis lake. Long easy cruising, more demanding pistes and dedicated fun zones make it a broad option for mixed-ability groups.

mf.label: Lifts including learning carpet
mf.note: One triple, two quads and one carpet.

ov.text: Val Saint-Côme mixes standard runs with an extensive glade offering, snow parks and ski-cross. Freestyle terrain is a visible part of its character, while the headline trail count combines several kinds of winter descent rather than groomers alone.

ov.text: Val d’Isère pairs demanding mountain skiing with designated quieter learning zones, Valkids and a freestyle park. Those options help families and mixed-ability groups find their own pace within a destination also known for its more challenging slopes.
Val-Louron is a family-oriented Pyrenees resort with a compact pedestrian base and approachable mountain terrain.

ov.text: Valberg combines alpine skiing with a lively village winter program near the Mercantour. The tourism office emphasizes terrain for different abilities and family outings, while Nordic skiing at Beuil-Les Launes is a separate part of the destination.

ov.text: Valdezcaray offers terrain from beginner pistes to difficult runs and separately listed off-piste itineraries. Chairlifts and drag lifts serve the mountain, with ski schools, rentals and food stops supporting a self-contained ski day in La Rioja.

ov.text: Valfréjus contrasts the easy pistes and play areas on Arrondaz with more demanding terrain around Punta Bagna. The long Jeu run provides another way back toward the village; nearby La Norma is reached by shuttle, not a connecting piste.

ov.text: Vall de Núria offers a small alpine network with green, blue, red and black pistes. Ski schools, a children’s piste and separate sledding activities support mixed family visits without requiring a large multi-mountain itinerary.
Valle del Sol is a small Spanish mountain ski area in the Sierra de la Demanda with local winter terrain.
Valloire is a traditional Maurienne village resort with varied alpine terrain and links toward neighboring Valmeinier.
Vallorcine is a quiet Chamonix-valley base linked into the Balme sector, with scenic terrain near the Swiss border.

ov.text: Vallter offers high-elevation skiing with green, blue and red pistes in a compact lift network. Its mixture of easier and more demanding runs supports progression, with complementary activities and visitor services around the resort.
Valmeinier 1800 is a purpose-built slopeside base with immediate access to the Galibier-Thabor ski domain.
Valmeinier is a Maurienne resort with village and slopeside bases connected into the wider Galibier-Thabor domain.
Valmeinier Villages represents the resort’s lower traditional settlements and their links toward the higher mountain network.

ov.text: Valmorel pairs a pedestrian village with varied local slopes and onward links through Le Grand Domaine, making architecture and mountain access equally distinctive.
Vars is a southern-Alps resort with high open bowls, village sectors and links across the Forêt Blanche domain.
Vassfjellet is a developed ski area near Trondheim, offering convenient regional access and varied groomed terrain.

ov.text: Velouchi Ski Resort offers open Greek mountain terrain above Karpenisi, with a sporting regional character and broad central-country views.
Ventasso Laghi is a northern Apennine mountain area with compact ski terrain in a scenic lake-and-forest setting.

ov.text: Verbier combines open, sunny cruising with more technical descents around its main mountain sectors. Access onward to Mont Fort and the wider Four Valleys makes it a base for longer explorations, while neighboring Savoleyres offers gentler alternatives.

ov.text: Vigla Pisoderi sits among beech woods at the meeting of the Varnountas and Verno ranges. Alpine pistes share the wider winter center with Nordic and snowmobile routes, so its overall route count is larger than the downhill ski inventory.

ov.text: Vihti mixes easy family slopes with race-oriented and harder runs, plus several park areas. Its position near Helsinki suits shorter outings and evening sessions; the gentle back slope offers a quieter-paced option for learning.
Villard-de-Lans is a major Vercors resort area combining village access, forested slopes and broad plateau scenery.
Villeneuve is a major Serre Chevalier base, linking developed slopeside services with the valley’s broad mountain network.
Vitsi is a Greek mountain ski centre near Kastoria with open regional slopes and a quiet highland atmosphere.
Voevodyno is a Carpathian resort where a small downhill area forms one part of a broader outdoor and lodging experience.

ov.text: Vogel offers natural-snow skiing above Bohinj in Triglav National Park, with mountain views, varied pistes and a snowpark. The full piste network depends on snow coverage, so the advertised maximum should not be mistaken for terrain available every day.

Vorlage is a village-based ski outing in Wakefield with an emphasis on family visits and learning. Evening and weekday pass options support regular local skiing; a trail-only pass is separate and does not include the lifts.

Voss links its train station to the mountain by gondola, making town-based ski trips practical. Family runs, race courses, parks and a night-lit network provide variety, with longer descents adding scale beyond the children’s areas.
VyshHora is a compact urban-edge ski area near Kyiv, focused on convenient lessons and short groomed laps.
Wakabuna Kogen offers a low-key Niigata mountain day with groomed slopes and an approachable local-resort pace.
Wakasa Hyounosen Ski Area combines western-Japan snow terrain with a regional mountain atmosphere and slopes for mixed abilities.
Wakkanai City Park is a small northern Hokkaido ski hill serving local recreation in an unusually coastal setting.
Warth-Schröcken is a snow-rich Arlberg resort area with high village bases and links into a much wider ski network.
Washigatake is a developed Gujo snow resort with broad groomed slopes and a lively regional destination feel.

Waterville Valley has an intermediate-heavy trail mix, with freestyle zones, learning programs and steeper options for progressing skiers. Its published ski acreage is distinct from the larger mountain property, keeping the scale of the downhill offering clear.

Welch Village offers a broad trail selection on a modest Minnesota vertical, with extensive snowmaking and a chairlift-heavy network. It suits repeat local laps from the Twin Cities or Rochester area without presenting itself as a high-alpine destination.
Welli Hilli is a developed South Korean mountain resort with groomed slopes and a substantial lodging base.

White Hills brings downhill skiing to the Clarenville area with a community-oriented mix of trails, lessons and rental equipment. Nordic skiing, snowshoeing and other winter activities sit alongside the downhill offer rather than increasing its trail count.

White Pass combines steeper runs off Great White Express with the broader exploration of Paradise Basin. Views toward Mount Rainier, a mid-mountain meeting lodge and slopeside lodging give it a relaxed mountain-trip character alongside its learning facilities.
White Pia Takasu is a developed Gujo snow resort with broad groomed slopes and connections within a larger regional ski cluster.

White Valley combines family practice and a forest descent with natural terrain on its upper slopes. Special Premium Powder Days change how much upper terrain is groomed, so the powder-focused offering depends on the operating program and conditions.

ov.text: Oze Iwakura combines gentle family runs and long intermediate cruising with steeper sporting terrain. Its race-oriented courses and ungroomed options provide a substantial contrast to the lower learning slopes, rather than a uniformly easy mountain.
Whitecap Mountain is a northern Wisconsin ski area with several forested peaks and an independent regional atmosphere.

Whiteface offers a long lift-served descent, an intermediate-heavy trail network and substantial expert terrain. The Slides add a separate, condition-dependent challenge above the lifts; their extra vertical and acreage are not folded into the lift-served headline.

ov.text: Whitefish combines 110 named trails with 3,000 acres and more than 2,300 feet of vertical. Its scale offers a large mountain network rather than a small cluster of short runs.

ov.text: Whitetail Resort offers a substantial Mid-Atlantic drop with terrain parks and pistes spanning beginner through expert difficulty.

Whitetail arranges beginner terrain on one side and expert runs on the other, making its progression-oriented layout easy to understand. Fully lit trails and extensive snowmaking support evening skiing as well as day trips.

ov.text: Whitewater leans strongly toward advanced skiing, with bowls, glades and expert runs defining much of its trail mix. Beginner and intermediate routes are also listed, but its in-bounds footprint is smaller than the broader total terrain promoted by the resort.

Wild Mountain puts learning and regular local participation at the center of its winter offering, with youth lessons, adult programs, racing and freestyle coaching. Its Taylors Falls site also has summer attractions, which are separate from the ski experience.
Willingen is a major German upland ski area with several local sectors, snowmaking and a lively resort-town setting.

Wilmot is a compact day-and-night ski area on the Wisconsin state line. A fairly even split of beginner, intermediate and advanced trails supports progression, with snowmaking across the terrain and a long-established ski school.
Winghills Shirotori is a Gujo mountain resort with gondola access, developed groomed terrain and a broad regional appeal.

ov.text: Wintergreen pairs Blue Ridge skiing with evening sessions and a freestyle park designed for progression. Snowmaking supports the ski terrain, while tubing is a separate activity rather than additional ski runs.

ov.text: Winterplace emphasizes learning and easy access near Interstate 77, with beginner and intermediate slopes making up most of its terrain. Night skiing and terrain parks extend the options, while its separate tubing park serves non-skiers.

ov.text: Wisp is a Western Maryland outing with a balanced mix of beginner, intermediate and advanced runs. Lighting and snowmaking cover much of the reported ski terrain, but the operator publishes incompatible acreage totals that still need clarification.
Witów is a compact Podhale ski area with family terrain and wide views toward the Western Tatras.

ov.text: Wolf Creek combines gentle learning slopes and intermediate groomers with extensive trees, bowls, chutes and ridgelines. Its family-run character and varied terrain give mixed-ability groups options, while expert sections retain a more natural, off-piste feel.

Now operating as Hatley Pointe, the former Wolf Ridge pairs a compact mountain with challenging runs, night skiing and slopeside dining. Public access uses online reservations and limited capacity, giving the experience a deliberately small-scale feel.
Wolzenalp offers small-scale Toggenburg skiing with natural-snow character and an unhurried local atmosphere.

Yabuhara offers a varied course network in the natural setting of Oku-Kiso. Its ski school supports children and adults developing their skills, while the mountain’s mogul events add a more technical side to the experience.
Yabuli Ski Resort is a major Chinese winter-sports destination with multiple mountain sectors, training heritage and a developed resort base.

Yachiho combines a short family learning slope and longer gentle cruising with broad carving terrain. A dedicated mogul run and short, steeper Trial course provide more demanding alternatives, while woodland and park features add playful variety.
Yad Moss is a volunteer-run English ski area with exposed Pennine terrain and operation governed by natural snow.

Yakebitaiyama combines gondola-served cruising with Olympic and steeper wall terrain within Shiga Kogen. It offers a substantial local day’s skiing while retaining links to the wider pass network; these measurements describe this mountain, not all Shiga Kogen.
Yakushi Ski Area is a compact Niigata community mountain focused on approachable slopes and uncomplicated local skiing.
Yam is an Iranian regional ski area with open mountain slopes and a straightforward local-resort character.
Yamada Onsen Kids Snow Park is a tiny family learning area where children, first turns and snow play are the entire focus.

Yamaboku uses rolling pasture and woodland terrain for a mix of gentle practice, groomed cruising and demanding ungroomed lines. Natural features give the slopes variety, but separately accessed touring routes are not counted as ordinary lift-served runs.

Zao Onsen is a major Japanese mountain resort combining an extensive lift network with a historic hot-spring town.
Yangdok is a North Korean mountain resort combining lift-served winter slopes with a purpose-built hot-spring complex.
Yawata Highland 191 is a compact western-Japan snow area with groomed cruising and a family-friendly regional atmosphere.

ov.text: Yeti starts at the top: visitors enter above the slopes and ski down toward the lifts. Its Mount Fuji setting combines a long learning-oriented route with shorter, harder courses and park features, giving beginners and improving riders different options.
Yogo Kogen is a Shiga ski area with developed regional slopes in a snow-prone northern mountain setting.
Yokone is a compact Japanese regional ski hill with a straightforward layout and low-key local character.
Yokoteyama–Shibutoge is a high Japanese mountain area with exposed upper slopes and links across the Shiga Kogen region.

Yomase combines learning slopes, longer main runs and dedicated pole-practice terrain. Its connection with X-JAM broadens the day’s choices, but the neighboring area’s park features and courses are kept separate from Yomase’s local inventory.
Yonezawa is a Yamagata ski area with groomed regional terrain and convenient access from the nearby city.

ov.text: Yongpyong combines short learning slopes with longer intermediate cruising and a broad lift network. Rainbow Paradise offers a sustained mountain journey, while the separate sledding slope and resort property area are not treated as downhill ski terrain.
Yumenotaira is a compact Japanese ski area with gentle regional terrain suited to family outings and repeat local laps.
Yunodai is a compact Japanese ski area with community-scale terrain in a regional snow-country setting.

Yunomaru organizes its skiing around a network of chairlifts with several nearby rest houses and lodging options. Ski and snowboard instruction supports practice days, while on-site hot-spring facilities offer a different pace after the slopes.

Yuzawa Kogen combines a lower learning area with ropeway-accessed highland skiing and mountain views. Snow play and sightseeing add options for mixed groups, while the shared Snow Link pass reaches other resorts whose statistics are not included here.

ov.text: Yuzawa Nakazato combines gentle learning slopes and playful family features with markedly steeper mogul and ungroomed runs. Woodland connections and designated tree terrain add variety, while the beginner snow escalator offers an alternative to starting on a chairlift.
Zadní Telnice is a Czech Ore Mountains ski centre with several local slopes and a traditional regional character.
Zagroń is a family-oriented Beskid ski area at Istebna with a compact slope network and developed base facilities.
Zao Liza World combines highland cruising and broad views with a quieter identity than the larger neighboring Zao Onsen network.
Zarabie Sport is a small ski area at Myślenice offering convenient regional slopes near Kraków.
Zarosliak is a Ukrainian Carpathian mountain base associated with local lift-served skiing and access toward Hoverla.
Zavyalikha is a Russian Ural mountain ski area with a developed lift network and a regional destination role.
Zettersfeld is a sunny East Tyrol ski area above Lienz with open alpine slopes and broad mountain views.

ov.text: Zieleniec is a major Polish Sudetes resort with numerous local sectors and a developed mountain-village base.
Zillertal 3000 is a broad Austrian ski network linking several Mayrhofen-area mountain sectors.
Złoty Groń is a developed Istebna ski area with groomed family slopes and convenient village access.

ov.text: Zürs offers open alpine surroundings within the linked Arlberg network, with gentle groomed options as well as a strong off-piste tradition. Guided backcountry and heliskiing are separate undertakings, not extra ordinary piste mileage.
Zwardoń Ski is a compact Beskid area near the Slovak border with local groomed slopes and village access.
Zwieselalm is a Dachstein West mountain sector with scenic alpine cruising and views toward the Gosaukamm.
